text:
Aditya Rao: starting thread on pilot customer selection for Optimize guardrails gating. need 3–5 design partners to run Phase 2. criteria + what “success” looks like.

Miguel Santos: :eyes: yep. i can pull a list from CS + pipeline. do we want only current Optimize users or also prospects?

Aditya Rao: mostly current users for first pass (so we get real apply flows + real deltas). but 1 prospect that’s quality/audit sensitive could be good if they’ll actually run prompt sets.

Owen Phillips: from support side, i’d bias toward customers who (a) already escalated quality regressions and (b) will be loud if we get false blocks 😅. better to learn early.

Marissa Cole: +1. also need coverage across optimization types. quantization is highest risk; batching/caching can break formatting / ordering. ideally pilots cover: 
- 1 heavy quant user
- 1 tool-calling / structured output workload
- 1 long-context / variable prompt length workload

Paula Mendes: and tiers matter. we need at least one enterprise/dedicated tier for override workflow + audit logging expectations.

Miguel Santos: ok, top of mind candidates:
1) Northbridge Support (existing customer, had past quality escalation)
2) “Acme Fintech” (enterprise prospect, audit requirements, quality sensitive)
3) a couple mid-market SaaS folks using tool calling (i’ll DM names once confirmed)

Owen Phillips: Northbridge is a good pick. they’re already asking “prove you ran checks before config changes” (we had SUP ticket on audit logs). they’ll also care about retention.

Aditya Rao: perfect. for Acme, will they actually let us run their prompt set through our harness? even if anonymized?

Miguel Santos: they said they can share a reduced set + synthetic variants. they’re pushing hard on SOC2-ish audit trail + “who approved override”.

Marissa Cole: if we include a prospect, make sure we don’t overpromise: pilot = guardrails gating for Optimize applies, not bespoke eval authoring services.

Aditya Rao: agreed.

Paula Mendes: what’s our “success” definition for pilot? we should be explicit before we recruit.

Aditya Rao: draft success criteria (happy to edit):
- guardrails catch at least 1 real regression / risky proposal before it hits prod (or at minimum flag a known risky quant transition)
- false block rate acceptable (target <10% of applies blocked due to flaky/noise; rerun resolves most)
- eval latency p95 < 12 min for gating runs (so apply flow isn’t brutal)
- override used rarely and with justification (target <5% of applies; and approval/audit logs complete)
- customers report gating UI explanations are understandable (CSAT-ish qualitative)

Owen Phillips: add: “no surprise changes.” even during observe-only, customers shouldn’t feel like Optimize is silently changing behavior. comms + UI state matters.

Miguel Santos: +1 on messaging. we should also define what happens on timeout. last thing we want is a pilot customer seeing “timeout” and being stuck.

Marissa Cole: timeout policy per tier is still being finalized, but for pilot we can keep it conservative:
- default = blocked + rerun option
- enterprise = request override / manual approval path

Paula Mendes: for pilot specifically, i’d like us to page ourselves only when we see sustained timeouts/backlog (not on single job). otherwise we’ll drown.

Aditya Rao: makes sense. i’ll align w/ Sean on alerting for pilot.

Owen Phillips: can we also define “success” as: support can explain outcome from the UI + audit event without engineering help. if it takes 4 ppl to decode a failed gating, that’s not ready.

Aditya Rao: good one. “support-ready.”

Miguel Santos: logistics: how many applies per customer do we need for signal? if a customer only applies once a month, pilot won’t tell us much.

Marissa Cole: yep. selection criteria should include expected volume (e.g., >= 5 applies/week or at least active experimentation). otherwise we’re just testing the happy path.

Aditya Rao: let’s set “pilot eligibility”: 
- active Optimize usage OR committed to run 10+ simulated applies via API in 2 weeks
- willing to share prompt set (or let us use a Redwood-curated set tagged to their workload)
- ok with us running evals (costs covered by Redwood for pilot)

Owen Phillips: “costs covered” is key. otherwise they’ll try to disable it.

Miguel Santos: ok. i’ll draft outreach blurb with these bullets + timeline + ask for prompt sets. will route to you before sending.

Paula Mendes: also ensure we can segment by deployment mode. hosted vs dedicated vs private. even if Private isn’t in the first wave, dedicated capacity behaves differently for gating load.

Aditya Rao: for this pilot, i’d do: 2 hosted, 1 dedicated, 0 private (unless we find someone already running Private and willing to engage).

Marissa Cole: agree.

Owen Phillips: action items:
- Miguel: shortlist 5–6 candidates with volume + workload tags + tier
- Aditya: finalize pilot success criteria + enforcement stage (observe-only vs soft-block) for week 1
- me: sanity-check which customers are likely to escalate if blocked + make sure CS is looped

Aditya Rao: :thumbsup: i’ll add this to the rollout tracker. also attaching a quick doc link w/ the success metrics draft (wip): https://redwood-internal/confluence/x/guardrails-pilot-success

Miguel Santos: will aim to post shortlist EOD tomorrow.

Paula Mendes: pls include who the customer admin contact would be + whether they have an internal evaluation harness already. helps set expectations.

Owen Phillips: and note if they have compliance/audit needs (SIEM export etc). we can use that to validate the audit event payload early.

Aditya Rao: cool. keep updates in-thread.
